title.value: Geographical concentration of COVID-19 cases by social determinants of health in 16 large metropolitan areas in Canada – a cross-sectional study
title.justification: The title of the paper is extracted from its header, providing an accurate and concise summary of the study's focus.
title.quote: Geographical concentration of COVID-19 cases by social determinants of health in 16 large metropolitan areas in Canada – a cross-sectional study

extractions.description: This study examines the geographical concentration of COVID-19 cases across sixteen large metropolitan areas in Canada, focusing on how these cases are distributed according to social determinants of health. Using Gini coefficients and Lorenz curves, the study analyzes the impact of factors such as income, education, immigration status, and occupation on the spatial distribution of COVID-19, highlighting significant geographical inequalities and emphasizing the need for geographically-prioritized responses to manage transmission risk and resource allocation efficiently.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the social and geographical distribution of COVID-19 rather than on ecological or climate-related impacts or solutions. The central theme is public health and social determinants rather than sustainable development in the ecological or climate sense.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We quantified social determinants of geographic concentration of COVID-19 cases across sixteen census metropolitan areas (CMA) in four Canadian provinces.

primary_category.justification: The focus of the paper is primarily on public health analysis related to COVID-19, emphasizing social determinants rather than climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: Although a consistent feature across CMAs was concentration by proportion visible minorities, the magnitude of concentration by social determinants varied across CMAs.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not align with any specific sub-category related to climate or ecological sustainable development given its focus on public health and social determinants.
primary_sub_category.quote: The feature of geographical concentration of COVID-19 cases was consistent across CMAs, but the pattern by social determinants varied.

new_primary_category.justification: Given the focus on geographic concentration of COVID-19 cases and their relation to social determinants, a new category specifically addressing public health analysis within pandemic contexts is suggested.
new_primary_category.quote: These hotspots are largely defined along social determinants related to occupation, income, housing, and proxies for structural racism.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper focuses on analyzing disparities in health outcomes geographically according to various social determinants of health, which suggests the introduction of a new sub-category to accommodate such studies.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We quantified social determinants of geographic concentration of COVID-19 cases across sixteen census metropolitan areas (CMA) in four Canadian provinces.
